scope: Existing production advisory set only, reconciled against pinned upstream, inspected package bytes and bounded compiled entry. Original boundary-review report unchanged.

inputs.artifact_status: Build 2, unaccepted and superseded by planned nested-dependency closure repair. This review is not acceptance of the archive.

audit_reconciliation.counts_note: Eight means vulnerable package records, not eight individual advisories. npm metadata covers a larger workspace graph and is not the shipped package count. The initially inspected root-only provenance manifest had 141 entries; nested server/node_modules entries were omitted. Packaging worker is separately repairing inventory, cache and archive closure.
audit_reconciliation.artifact_closure_blocker: Inspected archive lacks server/node_modules/Ajv despite the bundle importing ajv/dist/2020.js. A non-starting artifact is not a security mitigation. Reachability assessment describes the bounded entry with required dependencies correctly present.

findings.name: compression
findings.source_based_assessment: Compression middleware is in excluded upstream app.ts. The shipped entry does not import compression and does not install its response middleware. The premature-close zlib-stream leak therefore has no identified activation path in the bounded entry.

findings.name: fast-uri
findings.source_based_assessment: Ajv 8.20.0 imports fast-uri. tool-validate creates Ajv without loadSchema and uses synchronous compile for schema identifiers/references; argument validation is off by default. No adapter URL allowlist, outbound host decision or fetch uses fast-uri. Caller-controlled schema parsing is possible if the persisted opt-in is enabled, but advisory SSRF/host-authority prerequisites were not established. Keep this required transitive dependency and patch it.

findings.name: ip-address
findings.source_based_assessment: Only identified production parent is socks. The bundled entry has no socks-proxy-agent import after dead-code removal. Provider dispatch always uses direct global fetch; inherited/stored proxy configuration cannot activate SOCKS. The advisory classifier and oversized-string paths were not identified in permitted requests.

findings.name: multer
findings.source_based_assessment: proxyRouter imports multer and constructs memoryStorage transcription middleware. Its upload handler belongs to /v1/audio/transcriptions, which the outer adapter rejects before parsing. Allowed chat uses express.json; no multipart middleware is mounted on that route. Disk-storage advisory additionally lacks its diskStorage prerequisite. Required static import means deleting multer alone would break startup.

findings.name: proxy-addr
findings.source_based_assessment: Express loads proxy-addr but defaults trust proxy to false. createMaslowApp never changes that setting, binds loopback and authenticates bearer tokens rather than client IP. The advisory requires a malformed trusted IPv6/mapped subnet; no such trust configuration is present. This is a route-specific mitigation, not a patched library.

findings.name: qs
findings.source_based_assessment: Express/body-parser load qs. The adapter rejects query-bearing URLs, leaves Express simple query parsing in place and installs only express.json, not urlencoded. No qs.stringify round-trip of request data was found in permitted handlers. Patched qs remains required by Express/body-parser.

findings.name: sharp
findings.source_based_assessment: normalizeMessageImages dynamically loads sharp even for text-only requests. The outer policy has already rejected image/image_url parts and permits only strings or text parts, leaving no image slot to decode. Thus the libheif/librsvg malicious-image prerequisites are blocked at this entry; native vulnerable libraries are nevertheless shipped and loaded. The caught missing-sharp path is a possible tested pruning option, not an implemented fix.

findings.name: undici
findings.source_based_assessment: Unused proxy-agent code is absent from the bundled entry; no npm undici import remains. Provider chat and catalog sync call global fetch with redirects rejected. Pinned Node 22.23.3 reports built-in undici 6.28.1, distinct from shipped npm undici 6.28.0. No WebSocket client or retry interceptor is used by permitted routes. Removing/upgrading the npm copy does not alter the built-in copy.

overall_assessment: No exploit of the listed advisories was established through the reviewed text/function and signed-catalog routes. Several vulnerable packages are loaded or shipped; boundary mitigations and absent prerequisites do not make those versions fixed or clear the dependency gate.

recommendation.preferred_minimal_lock_option: After coordinator approval of the pinned-lock exception, refresh only the eight listed package resolutions to their compatible remediation targets, preserving upstream application revision and existing declared ranges. Recompute integrity/provenance and review the exact lock delta; avoid an unrestricted npm audit fix.
recommendation.pruning_alternative: The actual bundled entry has no compression, npm undici or socks-proxy-agent imports. These roots and only exclusively owned transitives, including ip-address, are candidates for deterministic production-closure exclusion. Do not remove shared transitives. Regenerate inventory and prove startup, text, functions, catalog and rejection behavior from the resulting archive.
recommendation.sharp_option: Sharp remains a dynamic import; its missing-module handler returns unchanged messages. Excluding sharp and matching native optional packages is plausible for the text-only product but requires explicit closure choice and artifact regression verification. Otherwise update sharp to 0.35.5 and refresh its platform/native dependencies.
recommendation.required_imports: Keep Express/proxy-addr/qs, Ajv/fast-uri and multer unless separately reviewing code changes to eliminate imports. They cannot be safely deleted from the existing bundle.
minimum_followup: Fix nested server dependency inventory/copying first.
Apply reviewed compatible lock changes or justified deterministic pruning.
Run production advisory query again against the exact closure; do not claim a clean result from this report.
Rebuild archive and verify manifest includes every nested/optional shipped dependency.
Recheck bounded bootstrap, authenticated text/function/SSE, fetched/cached catalog and rejected media/admin/proxy routes.

limits: No package/dependency install, cache mutation, code change, lock change or build was performed.
Read-only archive/source inspection and primary GitHub advisory verification; no exploit reproduction was attempted.
No provider request, private credential, account access, live setup, hardware or release gate was accepted.
Compatibility targets are supported by existing semver ranges and advisory patched versions, not tested upgraded dependencies.
New package/source bytes require affected review evidence to be regenerated.
